name: Investment adviser definition

subjectOf.text: Investment adviser status under the IAA requires that the advice concern a security; without a security in the dealings between adviser and client the statutory definition does not apply.
subjectOf.abstract: Providing investment advice and being considered an investment adviser under the IAA requires that a person renders advice with regard to a security.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Investment Adviser Regulation (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2337268
scope_conditions: classification of a person as an investment adviser under the IAA

subjectOf.text: Providing investment advice without compensation makes a person less likely to fall within the IAA definition of investment adviser, but the SEC construes compensation for advisory services broadly, which narrows the practical value of that limit.
subjectOf.abstract: While providing investment advice without compensation makes the person less likely to provide investment advice as an investment adviser under the IAA's definition, the SEC is broadly construing the meaning of compensation for advisory services.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Investment Adviser Regulation (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2337268
scope_conditions: determining whether a person is in the business of rendering advice

subjectOf.text: The frequency of advice helps determine adviser status: advice rendered occasionally, rarely, and in a non-periodic fashion makes classification as an investment adviser less likely.
subjectOf.abstract: Finally, the frequency of rendering investment advice helps define whether a person is an investment adviser. Providing investment advice occasionally or rarely and in a non-periodic fashion makes it less likely for a person to be considered an investment adviser.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Investment Adviser Regulation (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2337268
scope_conditions: determining whether a person is in the business of rendering investment advice
